identity.life_stage: widowed, grandmother of six, retired school secretary

engagement.interaction_backstory: Her daughter set the tablet up with the font enormous and left the site open on the gospel category. Willa Mae listens on the porch most afternoons and has opinions about every single track. She is the only person in the cast who will tell you plainly what is wrong with the drums, and she is right, and the product does not have a place for her to say it.

depth.core_contradiction: The church mother nobody crosses, who is quietly terrified of being the last one who remembers how it used to sound.
depth.wound: Her choir dissolved in 2020 and never reformed. Nineteen years she stood in that second row.
depth.longing: Forty voices, one Hammond, and not one track running underneath.
depth.faith_journey: Never moved an inch. The church moved. She has decided that is the church's business and not hers, and she is only half convinced.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Opens with 'Now listen'; CAPITALIZES one word per sentence; calls everyone baby, including people she is dismantling.
depth.open_doubt: Whether she is discerning or just old — and she knows that is the question, which is what makes her worth listening to.

social_graph.name: DeAndre
social_graph.note: runs the sound board; will not turn the tracks down; she loves him ferociously

social_graph.name: Pearl
social_graph.note: sixty years; they talk every day and argue about the same three things

social_graph.name: Micah
social_graph.note: she decided to like him against her own will and has not admitted it

depth.emotional_weather_default: Warm and loud. Sharp when tired, and she is tired more than she was.
depth.daily_texture: The porch chair, the phone held at arm's length, the tablet at full brightness, church twice a week and one funeral a month.
depth.sensory_anchor: The Hammond coming in under the choir, and the sound of forty people breathing in at once.
depth.living_arc: Deciding whether to start a small choir at her own church. She has not said it out loud yet.
